Operating evidence for incomplete repeated-subject time courses. The Synthetic repeated-subject
time course experiment to assess the declared condition target contrasts CM with CTL. (A)
Target loading recovery at the disclosed absolute cosine threshold. (B) Mean recurrence of the
nominated discovery axis under condition-stratified complete-subject bootstrap. (C)
Estimability of the adjusted condition-by-time random-intercept-plus-slope model after target
recovery. Red circles are estimated probabilities; crosses mark a scientific quantity that was
not estimable and are positioned near zero without encoding a probability; hollow triangles at
the left margin independently mark partial execution. The analysis unit is one repeatedly
observed synthetic mouse; the design is four CTL and four CM mice intended at each of four
observed times; mouse identity, condition, and time remain explicit; the estimand is
standardized condition-by-time interaction; time is recorded as weeks (times 0, 1, 2, 3) in
synthetic study units; adjustment uses batch. 5 deterministic outer replicates and 5
complete-subject axis bootstrap refits per eligible replicate were requested. No visit is
imputed or treated as an independent animal. Complete trajectories removes no observations; One
internal visit missing removes cm1 at time 2; One mouse drops out removes cm1 at time 2, cm1 at
time 3; Two disease mice drop out removes cm1 at time 2, cm1 at time 3, cm2 at time 2, cm2 at
time 3. Recovery uses an absolute loading-cosine threshold of 0.90. This is disclosed synthetic
calibration evidence, not an acceptance result or universal sample-size rule.
